title: I built a mobile multiplayer Pirate open world game. Opus 5.5 / 1 month / No coding experience
author: cherrycrushsmash
selftext:
I work in tech but I've never written code. I wanted to see if I could use AI to build a decent game and take it all the way to the mobile app stores.

It took about a month in my free time. Roguesail Raiders is an open world pirate game with up to 12 players in a voyage (6 ships, each with a captain and a crew mate). It's free with no ads, and you can play it in your web browser on a phone or computer, or try the iPhone and Android beta apps.

Play in your browser: [https://roguesailraiders.com](https://roguesailraiders.com/) (tap Set sail)  
Get the iPhone or Android beta: [https://roguesailraiders.com/beta](https://roguesailraiders.com/beta)

You start in a little sloop, raid merchant ships, fight other players and find buried treasure, slowly upgrading your ship all the way to a man-o'-war. Eventually you can earn enough gold to leave piracy behind and govern your own port, building it up like a builder game. There are sword fights ashore, a navy fort, and special monsters roaming the seas: the White Whale, the Kraken, a ghost ship at night, and a volcano that erupts mid-round.

How I built it: Claude Code running Opus 5.5 was basically my whole dev team. I described what I wanted in plain English and it built everything: the 3D game, the multiplayer server, accounts and leaderboards, and the mobile apps. It writes tests for its own work, plays the game in a browser to check things, and deploys when I say so. It also helped with the non-code stuff: checking the name wasn't taken, the privacy policy, and figuring out what the app stores need. Meshy made the 3D captain and Google Flow made the music. I mostly developed this from my phone with a remote session into my Claude Code desktop lol.

Would love any feedback, and happy to answer questions about the workflow.
